title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 153
paragraphs: Then in the twentieth month a prodigy befell Zopyros, son of that Megabyzos who had been one of the seven men who killed the Magian. To this Zopyros, son of Megabyzos, a prodigy occurred: one of the mules that served as bearers of provisions for him gave birth. When this was reported to him, and Zopyros had himself seen the foal—for he did not believe the report—he charged those who had seen it to tell no one what had happened, and he considered with himself what to do. Bearing in mind the words of the Babylonian who had said at the start that when mules bore young the wall would be taken—remembering, I say, this ominous saying—it seemed to Zopyros that Babylon could be taken. For he thought that both the man had spoken and his mule had foaled by divine dispensation.
